newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas eases on lack of demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas eases on lack of demand.

text.p: Singapore's gasoline prices slipped lower amid an abundance of supplies and a lack of sale outlets, traders said on Friday.
A major was heard to be bidding a cargo of 92 octane gasoline for May loading at $23.75 per barrel but there was a lack of keen sellers.

The major said there was some buying interest for high octane material from China and the company seeks to blend the 92-octane cargo to meet Chinese requirements, citing a lack of discussion for 95 and 97-octane gasoline.
Traders said Chinese demand were weak and bids were low.
But one trader was heard to be interested to buy 97-octane supplies for May loading but price details were unclear.
Most traders were sidelined awaiting fresh factors that would contribute to a clearer market direction.
Premiums in the Singapore market was assessed at around a $1.00 per barrel discount to Singapore spot quotes, free-on-board.
Talk in the naphtha market was further subdued by a holiday in Japan.
Naphtha swaps for May and June were quoted at $21.15/$21.25 and $21.40/$21.50 little moved from Wednesday's quotes.
Traders said the arbitrage window from the west is still open. They said this would add pressure to prices in Singapore.
Singapore refiners were mostly quiet with hardly any firm offers seen.
Fob premiums in the Singapore market is assessed at between 30 and 60 cents per barrel over spot quotes.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
